newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian house prices doubled in 6 yrs - minister.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian house prices doubled in 6 yrs - minister.

text.p: House prices in Malaysia have doubled over the past six years, Deputy Finance Minister Wong See Wah was quoted as saying by The Star newspaper on Tuesday.
Wong said this while releasing the National House Price Index, which is aimed at monitoring house price movements in the country.
A house costing 100,000 ringgit ($40,388) in 1990 would now cost around 212,000 ringgit, Wong said.
The estimated 20 percent annual growth could be the result of higher purchasing power among Malaysians, he added.
"At the end of 1995, total demand for ... houses was 4.9 million units, while the supply was only 4.5 million units," Wong was quoted as saying.
The index comprises eight categories which were drawn up after a study of 170,000 house transactions since 1988, he said.
"The study also revealed that the percentage increase in house prices over the past two years was more than the increases in the average incomes of housebuyers," he was quoted as saying.
